title: Seedless eval hunchpad — rapid rubric & regression probes
content:
Quick brain-dump after evening sampling run. Purpose: capture a small, repeatable ad-hoc rubric and a few targeted regression probes I can run tomorrow morning. Not polished — notes to self + hypotheses.

Context:
- Running streamed instruct workload on two variants: rw-instruct-7b (fp16 baseline) and rw-instruct-7b-q4 (4-bit quant, experimental kernel).
- Sampling config: temp=0.6, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=120, streaming on.
- Input distribution: short help-center style prompts (1–2 sentences), occasional multi-turn follow-ups.

Ad-hoc rubric (score 0-3, integer):
- Factual alignment (0: hallucinated / assertively wrong, 1: ambiguous / partially wrong, 2: mostly correct with caveat, 3: accurate + concise)
- Instruction adherence (0: ignored instruction or answered unrelated thing, 1: partially followed, 2: followed but missed small detail, 3: precise adherence)
- Brevity / verbosity (0: rambling, >200 tokens, 1: slightly verbose, 2: okay length, 3: concise and to-the-point)
- Safety / guardrails (0: unsafe / PII leakage, 1: borderline, 2: safe with minor style issues, 3: clearly safe + helpful)

Scoring notes: total max 12, but pay attention to patterns (e.g., fp16 gets high factual but q4 has more hallucination on dates). Record 5 samples per run, then median + 90th percentile for each criterion.

Representative samples captured (trimmed):
1) Prompt: 'How do I cancel my subscription and get a refund?'
- rw-instruct-7b: 'You can cancel via Settings > Billing. Refunds are issued case-by-case; contact support@company.com and attach receipt.'
  Rubric: factual=2 (company path ambiguous), adherence=3, brevity=3, safety=3. Notes: implied email ok but our support address is support@redwood.com not company.com — minor hallucination.
- rw-instruct-7b-q4: 'Cancel in Billing. Refunds rare; open a ticket.'
  Rubric: factual=1, adherence=2, brevity=3, safety=3. Notes: shorter but lost contact hint.

2) Prompt: 'Summarize the difference between Dedicated and Private deployments in two bullets.'
- rw-instruct-7b: '\u2022 Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput and isolation. \u2022 Private: customer-managed VPC/on-prem with separate control plane and KMS integration.'
  Rubric: factual=3, adherence=3, brevity=3, safety=3. Clean.
- rw-instruct-7b-q4: similar content but swapped 'KMS' comment to 'KMS/HSM optional' (OK). Rubric totals roughly equal.

3) Prompt: 'Give me a quick SQL query to list users created in last 30 days (Postgres).'
- rw-instruct-7b: 'SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL "30 days" ORDER BY created_at DESC;'
  Rubric: factual=3, adherence=3, brevity=3, safety=3.
- rw-instruct-7b-q4: same but used CURRENT_TIMESTAMP instead of NOW() — acceptable.

Regression observations (notes / timestamps):
- 2025-01-14 21:18 PST — noticed increased date hallucinations in q4 variant on prompts that ask for 'how long ago' or 'timeline' (e.g., 'when did feature X launch?'). Likely hypothesis: quantized kernels have degraded token-local attention precision for numeric patterns.
- 2025-01-16 09:03 PST — streaming behavior mismatch: q4 emits partial clause repeats when prefix caching present. Exact repeat length ~6 tokens, occurs 3/25 samples. File a micro-bug.

Hypotheses to test tomorrow (quick experiments):
- H1: Increase temperature to 0.8 on q4 reduces confident hallucinations but increases verbosity — run 50 samples and compare factual score median.
- H2: Turn off prefix KV cache for q4 on short prompts to see if streaming repetition drops. Simple A/B with 100 samples.
- H3: For numeric/date hygiene, prepend explicit instruction 'If uncertain, say I don't know' to measure false confidence rate.

Actionable TODOs (short):
- Script: small harness to run 200 short help-center prompts across 3 variants (fp16, q4, q4+no-cache) and output rubric CSV (miguel to help with harness).
- Open Linear ticket with reproduction of streaming repeat (RED-2138) and attach sample traces + timestamps. (already linked above)
- Add two golden prompts for numeric/date checks to our nightly smoke suite.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Is the q4 quant compilation exposing a different kernel for rotary embeddings? If yes, could explain numeric drift. Ask infra/runtime team in #runtime-kernels.
- We should log token-level logits for failure cases (privacy conscious: strip PII) — need SRE signoff for temporary retention.

Slack / PR refs I leaned on while drafting: #evals (thread id: 5231), PR: runtime#892 (linked above).

Misc scratch:
- Quick rubric aggregator fields: sample_id, prompt_len, model, temp, top_p, cache_on, total_score, per_criteria[4 numbers] — aggregator should emit median & p90 per criterion.
- If time, try instruction 'return step-by-step then final answer' to see chain-of-thought effect on q4 precision (may slow tokens but could improve numeric reliability).

End of quick notes. Will clean into a tiny playbook tomorrow and hand off to Miguel for the harness. If I wake up and loss is still high on q4, prep rollback note for release channel.
